To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lymph node dissection has a positive influence on the prognosis of colon cancer.
the prognosis of colon cancer patients is significantly improved by radical lymphadenectomy and that the quality of the histological examination has an essential influence on this result.
the prognosis of patients with colon carcinoma is improved by radical lymph node excision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fact that the quantity of lymph nodes excised is an important prognostic factor in the curative surgical treatment of colon carcinoma.
the fact that a radical lymphadenectomy is necessary for patients with colon carcinoma.
the question of whether the quantity of lymph nodes is an important factor of the prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in patients with an early stage of colon carcinoma (pT1-2 pN0) a radical lymphadenectomy has to be performed, in patients with an advanced tumor stage (pT3-4 pN0, pN1) a radical lymph node excision is necessary.

the radical lymphadenectomies in the early stages of colon carcinoma have no influence on the prognosis, but in patients with an advanced local tumor growth or with a lymph node metastasis the radical lymphadenctomies have a positive influence on the prognosis.
in the treatment of colon carcinoma the radical lymphadenectomies should be the method of choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of the histological examination of lymph nodes is essential for a correct staging.
a radical lymphadenectomy has to be carried out for all patients who are candidates for a curative operation.
a radical lymph node excision has to be performed in every patient with colon carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of lymph node excisions is essential for the evaluation of the prognosis in colon carcinoma.
lymphadenectomy should be performed in the treatment of colon carcinoma.
the number of lymph nodes removed is a good prognostic parameter in patients with colon carcinoma and should be increased in every case.
